_meta.name: Commodore 64 Open Source Code Corpus
_meta.purpose: Source-code-bearing companion to c64_resource_catalog.json. Where the first catalog gives Claude Code 'what the chip does and what tools exist', this gives it 'how good practitioners actually write games and demos'. Designed as training/grounding data for autonomous game and demo development against the c64-kb.
selection_criteria: Author-released originals (highest signal — author's own intent visible in comments and structure)
Reverse-engineered classics with build chains (mid-high signal — modern annotator's understanding overlaid on shipping production code)
Pedagogical samples bundled with explanatory articles (highest pedagogical signal — code + rationale together)
Reusable engines/frameworks (high signal for architecture patterns)
Snippet collections (low individual signal, high collective coverage of small techniques)
rejection_criteria: Demos labelled 'source available' but with source actually behind dead links

schema.name: human display name
schema.type: original-release | reverse-engineering | tutorial-sample | engine-framework | tool-source | technique-isolate
schema.form: game | demo | intro | engine | library | snippet-collection | tutorial-series | tool
schema.author: primary author (handle / real name)
schema.language: 6502-asm | KickAssembler | ACME | ca65 | xa65 | 64tass | C-cc65 | C-Oscar64 | C-LLVM-MOS | C++ | mixed
schema.completeness: full-game | full-demo | demo-version | engine-only | snippet | technique-isolate
schema.techniques_demonstrated: tags aligning with c64-kb technique entities
schema.pattern_signals: where in the repo each technique lives (path hints)

_meta.consumption_pattern_for_claude_code: For a generative task ('build a side-scrolling shooter'), the harness should: (1) identify required techniques from kb schema; (2) for each technique, query this catalog for entries where techniques_demonstrated contains that technique, ranked by code_quality and pedagogical_level; (3) ingest source from highest-ranked matches first; (4) treat author comments and companion_article URLs as ground truth for *why* a pattern is implemented a given way; (5) prefer recent originals over older reverse-engineerings when style hints conflict (modern authors comment intent; original 80s code is mostly uncommented).

resources.name: Hessian — full game source
resources.author: Cadaver / Lasse Öörni (Covert Bitops)
resources.ingest_notes: Likely the single highest-value full game source on GitHub: shipping commercial-quality game, MIT licensed, author also wrote canonical tutorials on the very techniques used. Cross-reference comments in hessian/ with cadaver.github.io/rants/ for intent.

resources.name: Steel Ranger — demo version source
resources.author: Cadaver / Lasse Öörni
resources.ingest_notes: Author noted on Lemon64 'may not be exactly learning-friendly' — meaning the code is dense and assumes the reader already understands the framework. Pair with c64gameframework for the more documented path.

resources.name: c64gameframework — engine + example
resources.author: Cadaver / Lasse Öörni

pattern_signals.level-data-tiling: 256 chars and 256 2x2 blocks model — see worldedit.txt

resources.ingest_notes: Modified version is what powers MW ULTRA. Example game is a simplified Steel-Ranger-asset platformer. Best documented Cadaver codebase — the README is essentially a brief textbook. Tooling (custom sprite/world editors) included.

resources.name: Metal Warrior 4: Agents of Metal — source
resources.author: Cadaver / Lasse Öörni
resources.ingest_notes: Older than Hessian/Steel Ranger; pre-c64gameframework era. Useful for understanding the evolutionary path of Cadaver's engine code.

resources.name: Covert Bitops Loadersystem (V3.x)
resources.author: Cadaver / Lasse Öörni
resources.ingest_notes: Game-oriented IRQ loader with Exomizer3 integration. Smaller and faster than V2 (used in Hessian/SR). 1541/71/81/CMD-FD/CMD-HD + SD2IEC (ELoad) support.

resources.name: oldschoolengine2 — Unity-side minimal C64 emulator
resources.author: Cadaver / Lasse Öörni
resources.ingest_notes: Not C64 code per se, but useful reference: shows exactly which C64 features Hessian/Steel Ranger actually depend on (the emulator implements only the subset needed). Implicit dependency map.

resources.name: Cadaver's coding rants
resources.author: Cadaver / Lasse Öörni

pattern_signals.sprite-multiplexing-radix-sort: sprite.html — referenced in Metal Warrior 3 source + BOFH source linked from page
pattern_signals.sid-playroutine-custom: music.html + custom routines in Metal Warrior series

resources.ingest_notes: Pair every Cadaver source repo with the matching rant. Rants give the why; source gives the how. Several rants link directly to .zip downloads of standalone example code (e.g., multi.zip).

resources.name: Corescape — vertical scrolling shmup
resources.author: drmortalwombat
resources.ingest_notes: Proves complex shmup is viable in C/C++ when targeting Oscar64. Pair with oscar64 compiler README claims about codegen quality.

resources.name: Minotrace — raycasting lab racer
resources.author: drmortalwombat

pattern_signals.raycasting: main C source — Wolfenstein-style fixed-point raycasting

resources.ingest_notes: Demonstrates that raycasting is feasible on C64 within real-time budget when written in optimizing C. High-signal for any 3D-on-C64 ambitions.

resources.name: Plekthora — horizontal shoot'em up
resources.author: drmortalwombat
resources.ingest_notes: Asm rather than Oscar64 — useful counterpart to other drmortalwombat games for comparing language-level overhead.

resources.name: OscarTutorials — small tutorial sources
resources.author: drmortalwombat
resources.ingest_notes: Bite-sized examples teaching Oscar64 idioms. Best starting point for an agent learning the C-on-C64 paradigm.

resources.name: oscar64 — bundled samples/games and tutorials directories
resources.author: drmortalwombat
resources.ingest_notes: samples/games/breakout.c is ~self-contained and demonstrates the canonical Oscar64 game-loop pattern: charset embed, rasterirq.h usage, sprites.h, sid.h. Highest pedagogical density per byte. Plus reference manual (oscar64.md) explains every C/C++ extension Oscar64 uses (banked memory, #embed, etc.).

resources.name: T-Rex 64 — Chrome dino clone
resources.author: Maciej Małecki

pattern_signals.copper-emulation: heavy use of c64lib/copper64 library for raster effects
pattern_signals.build-orchestration: build.gradle — modern Gradle plugin pipeline for a 6502 project

resources.ingest_notes: Showcase project for c64lib + Gradle Retro Assembler — the modern KickAssembler way. Build tool itself is significant: shows how to bring contemporary DevOps to retro coding.

resources.name: Tony: Montezuma's Gold — demo source
resources.author: Maciej Małecki (Monochrome Productions)
resources.ingest_notes: Commercial-release-quality Aztec-themed platformer; source for the free demo version was published Oct 2023. Heavy c64lib usage.

resources.name: Bluevessel — one-file intro / sample demo
resources.author: Maciej Małecki

pattern_signals.copper-list-style-rasters: uses c64lib/copper64 — Amiga-Copper-inspired raster macro library

resources.ingest_notes: Compact, comprehensible. Ideal 'hello world' tier intro source for Claude Code to start from when generating a one-filer.

resources.name: c64lib — KickAssembler library suite
resources.author: Maciej Małecki + contributors

pattern_signals.copper64: Amiga-style copper list / raster IRQ macro library
pattern_signals.text: text-mode macros for all 3 modes (standard, multicolor, ECM)

resources.ingest_notes: Multi-repo organisation. Most useful for building chip-level abstractions when generating Kick Assembler code. Each lib has docs at c64lib.github.io.

resources.name: Spindle source + example demo
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)

pattern_signals.scattered-loading: central design choice — see Operator's Handbook PDF

resources.ingest_notes: Spindle distribution includes the loader source + a full sample trackmo (.pef files + linker script). Read v3manual.pdf alongside. The Operator's Handbook is one of the best technical writeups in C64 history.

resources.name: Craft — C64 demo with full annotated source
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.ingest_notes: Custom-hardware-extending demo with extensive write-up. Mind-blowing technical density. Pair with the article on the page.

resources.name: A Mind Is Born — 256-byte demo
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.ingest_notes: 256 bytes total. Source + extensive write-up explain how a cellular automaton + LFSR generates both visuals and SID melody. The article is required reading for understanding 'every byte counts' optimization.

resources.name: Nine — sprite trickery demo + revelation article
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.companion_article: Linked from page — explains the 'seemingly impossible' effect
resources.ingest_notes: Modern (2025) demo with author-written revelation video and article showing exactly how the trick works. Ideal post-mortem for a Claude Code agent learning advanced sprite manipulation.

resources.name: Quondam Tunneling — fullscreen 3D tunnel + article
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.ingest_notes: Fjälldata 2026 tunnel-compo winner. Most recent lft demo — current state of the art for 3D-effect-on-C64 techniques.

resources.name: Lunatico — MISC effect article
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.ingest_notes: Introduced the MISC effect; article describes the technique in detail. Cite-worthy as the source for a named technique.

resources.name: Fast sprite Y-sort routine (article + code)
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.ingest_notes: Self-described as 'about as good as it gets' code by the author. One specific algorithm explained end-to-end.

resources.name: New pitch representation for SID playroutines (article)
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.ingest_notes: Generally relevant to building custom playroutines — addresses pitch resolution issues in conventional table-driven SID routines.

resources.name: Linus Åkesson programming articles (collection)
resources.author: Linus Åkesson (lft)
resources.ingest_notes: Index page. Crawl all article URLs. Each is a self-contained technique writeup with code.

resources.name: Uridium — reverse-engineered commented source
resources.author: Andrew Braybrook (original 1986); reverse-engineered by mwenge

pattern_signals.fast-scroll: src/scroll.s — Braybrook's famous high-speed scrolling routine

resources.ingest_notes: Builds from scratch on modern Linux/Windows. Comments are by the reverse engineer — explanations of *what* the code does, not always *why*. Cross-reference with Retro Gamer Issue 106 'Making of Uridium' for original-author intent.

resources.name: Morpheus — reverse-engineered source (Braybrook)
resources.author: Andrew Braybrook (1987); reverse-engineered by mwenge
resources.ingest_notes: Heavy use of Exomizer for the final build (Braybrook's data is compressed). Useful for understanding mid-late-80s Braybrook engine evolution post-Paradroid/Uridium.

resources.name: Iridis Alpha — reverse-engineered source (Jeff Minter)
resources.author: Jeff Minter (1986); reverse-engineered by mwenge

pattern_signals.preparatory-demos: demos/ folder includes Minter's DNA, Torus, Torus2 dev-stage demos

resources.companion_article: Iridis Alpha Theory — work-in-progress book on the codebase
resources.ingest_notes: Contains preparatory demos Minter released to friends on Compunet — windows into his iterative design process. Companion 'Theory' book is highly pedagogical.

resources.name: Llamasource — Jeff Minter games meta-collection
resources.author: Jeff Minter (originals); reverse-engineered by mwenge

pattern_signals.llamasoft-c64-assembly-patterns: dedicated overview document on common patterns

resources.ingest_notes: Includes a dedicated 'Common Patterns in Llamasoft C64 Assembly' overview — close to the actual c64-kb extraction target. Also a 'how to disassemble a C64 game' guide — directly relevant to your Rosetta64 work.

resources.name: Psychedelia — Minter's first light synthesizer (reverse-engineered)
resources.author: Jeff Minter (1984); reverse-engineered by mwenge
resources.ingest_notes: Cross-platform (C64, VIC-20, Atari 800 ports). Shows the same algorithmic core implemented across three 8-bit machines — relevant to Rosetta64 cross-platform analysis.

resources.name: Lode Runner C64 — reverse-engineered commented source
resources.author: Douglas Smith (1983 original); reverse-engineered by Piddewitt
resources.ingest_notes: Bit-for-bit identical reconstruction. Includes copy protection routine — interesting for understanding 80s anti-piracy schemes.

resources.name: Maniac Mansion C64 — mm-explained disassembly
resources.author: Lucasfilm Games / Ron Gilbert team (1987); reverse-engineered by pditincho

pattern_signals.scumm-c64-engine: main engine code — the SCUMM bytecode interpreter as implemented on C64

resources.ingest_notes: ~97% commented. Reveals the C64-specific implementation of SCUMM, including disk loaders. Educational/research only. Critically important for understanding script-driven adventure game architecture on 8-bit. Pair with ScummVM source for the modernized reimplementation.

resources.name: Elite (C64) — ca65-assemblable source
resources.author: Ian Bell + David Braben (1985); annotated by Mark Moxon
resources.ingest_notes: Recompilable. Part of a cross-platform family — Moxon maintains parallel annotated disassemblies for BBC, Apple II, NES versions. Comparison across versions is gold for Rosetta64-style code archaeology research.

resources.name: Mark Moxon's Elite source code family (cross-platform)
resources.author: Ian Bell + David Braben (originals); annotated by Mark Moxon
resources.ingest_notes: Repos for BBC/Acorn Elite, BBC Master Elite, Apple II Elite, NES Elite, plus support tools. Most exhaustively commented disassembly project anywhere — gold standard.

resources.name: leissa/c64engine — sprite multiplexer + open border engine
resources.author: Roland Leißa
resources.ingest_notes: Compact (36 raster lines CPU time / 33 raster lines screen space) but covers several techniques together. Good integration example.

resources.name: C64 Multiplexor C LIB (CC65 + KickAssembler)
resources.author: Fabrizio Caruso, Flavio Pasqualin, Antonino Porcino
resources.ingest_notes: Derived from Cadaver's multi.zip. Modernized as C-callable library — useful template for exposing low-level asm to C-level game code. Up to 36 multiplexed sprites.

resources.name: zendar/spritemultiplexer — tutorial multiplexer
resources.author: Zendar, after Cadaver
resources.ingest_notes: Tutorial walkthrough explaining each step of the multiplexer. Good starting point if Claude Code needs to build one from first principles before tackling Cadaver's production code.

resources.name: wizofwor/C64-assembly-examples
resources.author: wizofwor
resources.ingest_notes: Short single-purpose routines (IRQ multiplexer, color-bar, joystick read, music-in-BASIC). Bread-and-butter snippet collection.

resources.name: nealvis/c64_samples_kick + nv_c64_util
resources.author: Neal V
resources.ingest_notes: KickAssembler-centric. Companion utility library nv_c64_util provides reusable macros. Good Claude Code starting template for VSCode-based development.

resources.name: c64scene-ar/c64demo — Spindle-based demo template
resources.author: Various (c64scene Argentina)

pattern_signals.spindle-build-pipeline: Makefile per scene + scenes/ directory + scripts
pattern_signals.scene-chaining: src/script defines load order and inheritance flags

resources.ingest_notes: Reference template for building a multi-part trackmo with Spindle from scratch. Build infrastructure is the main value — once Claude Code can fork this and add new scene .pef files, it can produce trackmos.

resources.name: C64 Christmas Demo (celso/c64)
resources.author: Celso Martinho (Bright Pixel)
resources.companion_article: Article on github.com/celso/c64 README — walks through every section of the demo
resources.ingest_notes: Excellent first-look at Kick Assembler with companion essay. Single-author single-file, ideal starter.

resources.name: NUFLIX — pushing C64 graphics article
resources.author: Patai Gergely (cobbpg)
resources.ingest_notes: Deep technical writeup explaining NUFLIX picture format with code. Defines the cutting edge of static-image-on-C64 — relevant for any title-screen/cutscene work.

resources.name: Unfortunate Coincidence — sprites-only demo writeup
resources.author: Lethargy Dev
resources.ingest_notes: Process write-up rather than full source dump — but explains the trade-offs (multiplexer vs sprite stretching, etc.) very clearly. Useful for understanding *why* one technique gets picked over another under cycle pressure.

resources.name: Freedroid Classic — Paradroid GPL remake
resources.author: Andrew Braybrook (1985 original); GPL remake by Reinhard Prix et al.
resources.ingest_notes: Not a C64 disassembly but a portable C remake — useful for understanding *gameplay* logic separately from C64-specific implementation. Cross-reference for Paradroid before/until someone publishes a true C64 disassembly.

resources.name: RetroReversing C64 section
resources.author: RetroReversing community

pattern_signals.various-disassemblies: central index of C64 disassembly projects

resources.ingest_notes: Aggregator/index — points to many disassembly and reverse engineering writeups across the C64 space. Treat as a discovery surface, not a primary corpus.

resources.name: CSDb 'Source Code Included' filter
resources.author: Various scene authors
resources.ingest_notes: CSDb has dedicated release types for tools/sources. Many demos include a 'sources' download on their release page (e.g., csdb.dk/release/?id=N&show=sources). Scrape release detail pages for the 'sources' section. High-volume / variable-quality — filter by votes/scene group reputation.

resources.name: GitHub topic: kickassembler
resources.author: Various
resources.ingest_notes: Discovery surface for KickAssembler projects. Pair with topic:cc65, topic:oscar64, topic:c64-game, topic:c64-demo.

resources.name: GitHub topic: c64 + game-related tags
resources.author: Various
resources.ingest_notes: Filter by language=assembly + stars>=10 + recent push for the high-signal subset. Use GitHub API.

resources.name: mwenge GitHub — full disassembly index
resources.author: mwenge (collected from many original authors)
resources.ingest_notes: Treat the whole mwenge namespace as one corpus. Includes uridium, morpheus, iridisalpha, psychedelia, llamaSource, and more. All have consistent build chains and similar comment style.

resources.name: Selmiak C64 Tutorials site
resources.author: Selmiak
resources.ingest_notes: Newcomer-friendly walkthroughs in English. Good complement to Codebase64 which assumes more prior knowledge.

resources.name: Saetto / Saito C64 games (Trance Sector, etc.)
resources.author: Saetto / Saito
resources.ingest_notes: Source not always public but some releases include it on CSDb. Check per-release.

resources.name: Richard Bayliss / TND — free games and music
resources.author: Richard Bayliss (TND)
resources.ingest_notes: Prolific producer of free C64 games and demos for ~25 years. Source not consistently published but several releases include it. Long catalogue useful for understanding small-team production patterns.

resources.name: Cosine — long-running scene group releases
resources.author: Cosine (T.M.R. and others)
resources.ingest_notes: Long-running group; releases span 30+ years. Source occasionally bundled in releases — check CSDb release pages for 'sources' download.

resources.name: Smkx / various one-filer demos with source (CSDb)
resources.author: Various
resources.ingest_notes: Generic placeholder for the large body of one-file demos with source-included tagging on CSDb. Crawl by 'category=Demo' + tag-search 'source code'.

resources.name: ByteBoozer 2 — cruncher with C64 decruncher source
resources.author: HCL (Booze Design)
resources.ingest_notes: Useful for fingerprinting Booze Design / Censor / Resource releases that use it. Source download from CSDb release page.

resources.name: Exomizer source (host + C64 decruncher)
resources.author: Magnus Lind
resources.ingest_notes: exodecrs/ subdirectory contains the canonical C64 decrunchers in 6502-asm (multiple variants — backwards, in-place, mem). These are the routines embedded into half the C64 scene's releases.

resources.name: Krill's Loader — source distribution
resources.author: Krill / Plush
resources.ingest_notes: Extensively commented. Includes integration code for Exomizer, ByteBoozer, Doynax. Source is essentially a textbook on modern fastloader architecture.

resources.name: Bitfire — IRQ loader source
resources.author: Bbox / Bonzai
resources.ingest_notes: Alternative to Krill and Spindle. Different design trade-offs documented in source comments.

resources.name: Microsoft BASIC 6502 unified source (mist64)
resources.author: Microsoft 1977 / Commodore variants; curated by Michael Steil
resources.ingest_notes: Builds Commodore PET/VIC-20/C64/C128 BASIC ROMs from a single annotated source. Educational for understanding interpreter/REPL design on 6502.

resources.name: mist64/c64rom — original Commodore source archive
resources.author: Commodore / curated by Michael Steil
resources.ingest_notes: Original Commodore source code for the KERNAL/BASIC ROMs. Period-authentic comments. Best ground truth for KERNAL routine semantics — every game using $FFxx jump table assumes this code's behavior.

resources.name: Battle City — annotated 6502 disassembly + JS port
resources.author: Namco 1985 (Famicom); annotated by community
resources.ingest_notes: Famicom-targeted, not C64 — included as an example of 6502 game architecture that ports cleanly to web. Useful as a non-C64 6502 reference point for cross-platform analysis.

resources.name: Codebase64 source snippets (extracted)
resources.author: Codebase64 contributors (many)
resources.ingest_notes: Extract code blocks from Codebase64 as first-class corpus. Listed here in addition to the c64_resource_catalog wiki entry so that Claude Code's source-corpus queries find it. Each <pre class="code 6502"> block in the wiki becomes a snippet entity with technique tags inferable from the page title.

resources.name: VICE testprogs — emulator regression suite
resources.author: VICE team + contributors
resources.ingest_notes: Each subdirectory is a single-feature edge-case test program — minimal source isolating one VIC-II/SID/CIA behavior. Perfect for technique-grounding. Cross-reference with c64-wiki/codebase64 articles describing the same effect.

resources.name: Easy 6502
resources.author: Nick Morgan
resources.ingest_notes: Not C64-specific (uses a generic 6502 simulator) but the canonical entry-point for newcomers to 6502 assembly. Useful as the first link a Claude Code agent learning the basics would hit before specializing to C64.

resources.name: Millfork example programs
resources.author: Karol Stasiak
resources.ingest_notes: Millfork = a high-level language with 6502 semantics. Examples show idiomatic Millfork code for typical C64 patterns. Useful counterpoint to Oscar64 and cc65 idioms.

resources.name: cc65 — bundled samples and examples
resources.author: Ullrich von Bassewitz + contributors
resources.ingest_notes: Includes complete small games (e.g., gunzip65, Tetris-like, etc.) demonstrating cc65 + conio.h / joystick.h / tgi.h usage. The official 'how to use the cc65 stdlib' corpus.

resources.name: Retro Game Dev (Derek Morris) companion code
resources.author: Derek Morris
resources.ingest_notes: Companion code to the Retro Game Dev book series. Builds simple but complete games step-by-step. Designed for beginners — useful pedagogical scaffolding.

resources.name: Prince of Persia (C64 port) — popc64 project
resources.author: Andreas Larsson / Sintech (port team)
resources.ingest_notes: Multi-year reverse-engineering + port project, with dev blog documenting the journey. Use blog as primary intent-source, source code (if extractable from release builds) as implementation reference. Sintech's port adaptation of Mechner's released source.

resources.name: Prince of Persia (Apple II) — Mechner's released source
resources.author: Jordan Mechner
resources.ingest_notes: Apple II not C64, but same CPU and similar era. Highly significant for understanding 6502 game architecture from one of its acknowledged masters. Cross-reference with popc64 for the C64 adaptation choices.

resources.name: Freeload (Ocean fastloader) write-up (Paulie Hughes)
resources.author: Original: Jonathan Smith / Ocean; analysis: Paulie Hughes
resources.ingest_notes: Detailed analysis of the iconic Ocean Freeload — explains the rasterbars-during-load aesthetic and Martin Galway's loading-music integration. Cultural-context-heavy companion to the technical Krill/Spindle loaders.

_pedagogical_phase_ordering_for_autonomo._explanation: When the harness gives Claude Code a generative goal ('build a side-scrolling shooter using c64-kb'), ingest source in this order:
_pedagogical_phase_ordering_for_autonomo.phase_1_rationale: Beginner-pedagogical sources establish baseline pattern vocabulary (raster IRQ, sprite setup, joystick read, music init/play) in isolation. Each snippet is self-contained and demonstrates exactly one concept.
_pedagogical_phase_ordering_for_autonomo.phase_2_rationale: Mid-complexity engines and demo templates — multiple techniques composed together. Authors comment intent. Bridges from snippet vocabulary to full-game architecture.
_pedagogical_phase_ordering_for_autonomo.phase_3_rationale: Production-grade complete games by acknowledged masters, with full source. This is where Claude Code learns to *integrate* techniques — how a complete game balances raster time, memory, fastloader scheduling, and gameplay.
_pedagogical_phase_ordering_for_autonomo.phase_4_rationale: State-of-the-art demoscene work. Cycle-counted, often single-purpose, frequently inventing new techniques. lft articles especially: each one is essentially 'here's a technique I discovered, here's why it works, here's the code'. Treat as research papers in code form.
_pedagogical_phase_ordering_for_autonomo.phase_5_rationale: Reverse-engineerings of classics show how master practitioners of the 80s actually built shipping games under tight memory/time constraints. Comments are modern; intent is sometimes inferred. Excellent for understanding why some idioms exist (e.g., self-modifying code patterns that look weird in modern code but made cycle-budget sense in 1986).
_pedagogical_phase_ordering_for_autonomo.phase_6_rationale: The substrate beneath every C64 release. Understanding what KERNAL/BASIC ROMs actually do, how loaders work end-to-end, and how the crunchers chosen affect runtime structure, lets the agent reason about resource constraints holistically.

_cross_references_to_catalog_1.tooling: Every entry's `toolchain` field references a tool in c64_resource_catalog.json — e.g., 'KickAssembler' → resources[id=kickassembler], 'Oscar64' → resources[id=oscar64]. Resolve transitively when ingesting.
_cross_references_to_catalog_1.techniques: Every `techniques_demonstrated` tag should resolve to a technique entity normalized from codebase64 + c64-wiki + Christian Bauer's VIC-II doc. Build the technique entities from catalog 1 FIRST, then this catalog's source corpora become labeled examples of those entities.
_cross_references_to_catalog_1.people: Author handles (Cadaver, lft, drmortalwombat, mwenge, Mark Moxon, Maciej Małecki, Andrew Braybrook, Jeff Minter, Jordan Mechner) should each become a person entity. Many appear on CSDb — cross-link person.csdb_id where possible.

strongly_positive: Author also wrote the canonical tutorial article on the technique used (e.g., Cadaver's rants matching his game code; lft's articles matching his demo code)
Code builds with a modern toolchain (no archaeology required to ingest)
Recent commits (alive project, comments reflect modern understanding)
weakly_positive: GitHub stars > 50 (community endorsement, but not definitive)
CSDb release with high vote count
negative: Source only available as a binary blob inside a D64 (treat as needing disassembly first)
Last commit > 5 years ago AND no working build chain (likely bitrot)
Author explicitly says 'this is not learning-friendly' (Cadaver said this about steelranger-demo — caveat the ingestion)
Comments are in a non-English language with no translation (still useful but lower-priority for English-speaking agent)
